draft.title: The rise of environmental concern
card: In 1962 the American biologist Rachel Carson published Silent Spring. It warned that pesticides such as DDT were harming birds, other wildlife and the wider environment.
The book was widely read. It made many ordinary people ask whether human activity was damaging nature, and it led people to question how chemicals were used.
Worry about pollution of air, water and land kept growing in the 1960s. In 1970 the first Earth Day was held in the United States, with millions of people taking part in events and rallies.
Over the same years, new environment groups formed and existing ones gained members. They pushed governments and businesses to protect the natural world.
draft.remember: Silent Spring in 1962 and rising pollution worries led to Earth Day in 1970 and new environment groups.

a.q: What was the main warning of Rachel Carson's book Silent Spring?
opts: Pesticides were harming wildlife and the environment
Factories should be moved away from large cities
Forests were being cleared faster than they could regrow
Nuclear weapons tests were poisoning the oceans
a.why: Carson argued that pesticides such as DDT were harming birds and other wildlife. The other options are real environmental worries, but they were not the central warning of this book.
a.clue: Think about the chemicals used on farms and crops.

b.q: In 1971 Priya, a student in Melbourne, joins a new environment group after reading about pollution and the first Earth Day. Which change in thinking does her choice best show?
opts: Growing public concern about harm to the environment
Governments had already solved pollution problems
People believed pesticides were completely safe to use
Environment groups were only run by scientists
b.why: Priya's choice shows that more ordinary people were worried about pollution and were willing to act, as with the new groups of this period. Saying pesticides were seen as safe is wrong, because Silent Spring had raised doubts about them.
b.clue: Why would people be joining new groups at this time?

a.best: Pesticides were harming wildlife and the environment

b.best: Growing public concern about harm to the environment

problems.detail: The right option stands out by form. It is the only noun phrase, and it matches the stem's 'which change in thinking'. The three wrong options are full sentences built on absolutes ('only', 'completely', 'already'), so a student could pick the answer without knowing the idea.
